---
title: "Bias, Variance, and Nonlinear Models"
---

This lecture connects model flexibility to prediction error and then
introduces nonlinear regression tools such as polynomials, step
functions, splines, and generalized additive models.

## Learning Objectives

- Explain the bias-variance tradeoff.
- Identify underfitting and overfitting from train/test patterns.
- Fit polynomial, step-function, spline, and additive models.
- Use validation to choose nonlinear complexity.

## Core Ideas

Increasing flexibility often lowers bias and raises variance. The
practical question is not whether a model is flexible, but whether its
flexibility is earning lower expected test error.

For a new point $x_0$, the expected prediction error can be decomposed
as

$$
\operatorname{E}\{(Y - \hat f(x_0))^2\}
= \operatorname{Var}(\epsilon)
+ \operatorname{Bias}(\hat f(x_0))^2
+ \operatorname{Var}(\hat f(x_0)).
$$

The irreducible error $\operatorname{Var}(\epsilon)$ remains even for a
perfect estimate of the regression function. The reducible part depends
on the learning method, sample size, and model complexity.

## Nonlinear Regression Tools

Linear regression can represent nonlinear relationships by transforming
or expanding the predictors.

| Method | Model idea | Main tuning choice |
|---|---|---|
| Polynomial regression | Add powers such as $x^2$ and $x^3$ | Degree |
| Step functions | Divide a predictor into intervals | Cut points |
| Regression splines | Fit smooth piecewise polynomials | Knots or degrees of freedom |
| GAMs | Add smooth functions of multiple predictors | Smoothness per term |

```r
library(ISLR)
library(splines)
library(gam)

wage <- ISLR::Wage

poly_fit <- lm(wage ~ poly(age, 4), data = wage)
spline_fit <- lm(wage ~ bs(age, df = 6), data = wage)
gam_fit <- gam(wage ~ s(age, df = 5) + education + year, data = wage)
```

## Choosing Flexibility

Use validation or cross-validation to choose flexibility. Training error
usually decreases as models become more flexible, but test error often
decreases only until the model starts fitting noise.

## Nonlinear Function Comparison

Use a simulated nonlinear function and a real data example to compare
linear regression, polynomial regression, regression splines, and GAMs.

## Flexibility Practice

Practice by modeling a nonlinear relationship with polynomial terms,
step functions, regression splines, and a generalized additive model.
Use validation or cross-validation to choose complexity, then explain
which model balances flexibility and interpretability best.
